title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Benefits
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare. They say your benefits will be canceled unless you give them personal information, like your Medicare number or Social Security number.
example_message: "This is Medicare. We need to confirm your information or your benefits will be stopped. Please give us your Medicare number now."
red_flags: Caller says your benefits will be canceled immediately
Asks for your Medicare or Social Security number
Pressures you to act right away
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Fake Tech Support Pop-Ups on Your Computer
how_it_works: A pop-up appears on your computer saying you have a virus. It tells you to call a number for help. If you call, the scammer asks for money or remote access to your computer.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft Support now at 1-800-XXX-XXXX."
red_flags: Pop-up says you have a virus and gives a phone number
Asks for remote access to your computer
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number. If you need help, contact a trusted local computer repair shop.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts
how_it_works: You get a text message saying a package is waiting for you. The message asks you to click a link to reschedule or track the delivery. The link may steal your personal information or install malware.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Click here to schedule: [fake link]"
red_flags: Link asks for personal or payment information
Poor grammar or strange web address
what_to_do: Do not click the link. If you’re expecting a package, check with the delivery company directly.

title: Grandparent Emergency Scam
how_it_works: Someone calls pretending to be your grandchild or a lawyer. They say your grandchild is in trouble and needs money right away for bail or an emergency.
example_message: "Grandma, I’m in trouble and need money for bail. Please don’t tell mom or dad. Send money now."
red_flags: Caller says it’s urgent and asks for secrecy
Asks for money by wire transfer or gift cards
Won’t let you speak to your real grandchild
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member to check the story.

title: Social Security Suspension Email Scam
how_it_works: You receive an email saying your Social Security number is suspended due to suspicious activity. The email asks you to click a link or call a number to fix the problem.
example_message: "Your Social Security number has been suspended. Click here or call us now to reactivate your account."
red_flags: Threatens to suspend your Social Security number
Asks you to click a link or call a number
Email address looks suspicious or isn’t official
what_to_do: Do not click any links or call the number. Delete the email and contact Social Security at their official number if you’re concerned.
